findings.title: A figure a model returned was never checked against the ad it read
findings.repro: node test/benchmark.test.js  (STAGE 10). A model answer of { metric: "apy", raw: "6.75% APY" } over a description that prints no rate.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-001-before.txt — 7 failing assertions; `grounded` is undefined on every fact, and the invented 6.75% APY becomes the brand's advertised position and is ranked against the client.
findings.rootCause: observations.js describes itself as the gate between what a model PROPOSED and what may be COUNTED, and gated the metric registry, the product profile, completeness and rankability — but never whether the string appeared in the transcription the same model call produced. An invented figure is indistinguishable from a transcribed one once it is inside facts[].
findings.fix: isGrounded()/sourceTextOf() in observations.js, applied per creative (never per brand) to every fact's raw and every claim's verbatim; ungrounded entries are kept, marked, and excluded from positions, ranks and denominators, held in their own `ungrounded` map rather than in `partial` (which means 'the ad text was clipped' and would be false). extract.js grounds the display offer against its own transcription and withholds `numeric`, which is the gate strongestOffer(), the wall's offer counts and the cluster key all read.
findings.riskOfFix: A genuine figure whose transcription differs in form could be refused. Mitigated by normalising unicode, curly quotes, ellipsis and whitespace, and by a second whitespace-stripped pass. Two benchmark.test.js fixtures encoded reads that could not have happened and were corrected.
findings.testAdded: test/benchmark.test.js :: STAGE 10 (7 assertions), and the cross-cutting sweep in test/flow.test.js :: 'no finding cites a figure that is not in the ad it cites'

findings.title: productConfidence was computed, clamped, stored — and read by nothing
findings.repro: node test/flow.test.js :: 'a creative the reader could not place is captured, shown, and not counted'. PEL2 in test/fixture-lab.js is "Bank With Us", auto-loan, productConfidence 0.15.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-002-before.txt — "1.99% APR reached the snapshot from a creative classified at 0.15 confidence", and the audit table counted 2 ads where the board counted 1.
findings.rootCause: Both extractors compute and clamp productConfidence and nothing reads it, so a creative the reader explicitly marked as unplaceable entered the product's comparison beside one at 0.9.
findings.fix: PRODUCT_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.5 with the reasoning in a comment (0.5 is where both shapers park a read that returned no confidence, so the gate refuses only an ACTIVELY unsure read and never a missing field). filterByProduct gains an explicit `confident` option, passed at every counting boundary — buildBoard and buildBenchmark both, so the two cannot disagree. captureFunnel gains a fourth step rather than shrinking its third.
findings.riskOfFix: A correct read that reports low confidence stops being counted. This is the intended trade; it stays captured, on the wall, in the chips and in the funnel.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'a creative the reader could not place is captured, shown, and not counted' (6 assertions)

findings.title: /api/rate-pages would fetch any URL, including this machine
findings.repro: bughunt/logs/f008-concurrency-probe.mjs's sibling: stand up an http server on 127.0.0.1 and pass its URL to readRatePage().
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-003-before.txt — 'loopback hits: 1 / text was read: YES — the internal page's contents were fetched'. After: 0 hits, reason not_https.
findings.rootCause: No scheme check, no host check, no redirect check, no size or time cap on the body. The endpoint takes a URL from a form and returns what it finds.
findings.fix: checkPublicUrl() blocks loopback, 0.0.0.0/8, RFC1918, CGNAT, IETF assignments, benchmarking, multicast and reserved v4; ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10 and multicast v6; IPv4-mapped v6 in both spellings; and localhost, *.localhost, *.internal, metadata.google.internal by name. https only. redirect:"manual" with each Location re-validated from scratch, up to 3 hops. One AbortController over headers AND body, with the body read through a 3MB byte counter. Fails closed on a name that will not resolve. Resolver is injectable so the guard is testable with no network.
findings.riskOfFix: A rate page behind an http-only host, or on a name whose DNS is flaky, is now refused. Both surface as a per-domain reason in the UI, exactly like a failed capture.
findings.testAdded: test/degraded.test.js :: 'rate-page fetch refuses to read this machine' (20 assertions)

findings.title: A paid endpoint nobody could reach was still generating and billing
findings.repro: POST /api/run/:id/strategies against any finished benchmark run.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-004-before.txt — the route, the import, the dead client functions, and two tests that PROVED the generator still ran and returned angles.
findings.rootCause: The button was removed from the UI when the strategy pass was retired; the route, the generator and the client code stayed mounted.
findings.fix: Removed the route, generateStrategies, lib/strategies.js, wireGate()/strategyHtml() in public/app.js, and the '7-strategies' screenshot step that clicked a button that is not on the page. payload.strategies stays null so a saved run does not grow an undefined where a null used to be.
findings.riskOfFix: Anything still POSTing the old path gets a 404 instead of an answer. That is the point.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'the strategy gate is gone, not merely hidden' (2 assertions). The three strategy tests were deleted with the route.

findings.title: A run could finish, be paid for, save nothing, and report success
findings.repro: node test/degraded.test.js :: 'a run that could not be written says so'. The test puts a DIRECTORY where the run file wants to be, mid-capture.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-005-before.txt — 'persisted: expected false, got undefined'. The run reported done with ads on screen and nothing on disk.
findings.rootCause: saveRun() returned a boolean and not one of its four call sites read it, so an unwritable or full data directory produced one console line and a user told their capture completed.
findings.fix: writeAtomic() (temp file + rename) for run records, cached extractions and the manifest; persist() wraps saveRun at every call site and records the answer on the run; payload.persisted and one sentence on the results screen.
findings.riskOfFix: A rename across filesystems would fail where a write succeeded. The temp file is created in the same directory as its target, so this cannot arise.
findings.testAdded: test/degraded.test.js :: 'a run that could not be written says so' + 'a half-written run file is never left on disk' (6 assertions)

findings.title: The ACTIVE map had three .set calls and no .delete
findings.repro: node test/flow.test.js :: 'an evicted run reads back off disk unchanged', with RI_ACTIVE_RUNS=4 and six runs.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-006-before.txt — health reports no runsInMemory at all; nothing was ever evicted.
findings.rootCause: Every run ever captured stayed in memory for the life of the process, holding its full ad records.
findings.fix: LRU with a cap (RI_ACTIVE_RUNS, default 24). Never evicts an unfinished run (memory is the only copy) or one that failed to persist (F-005 — there is nothing to load it back from). remember() does delete-then-set because Map.set keeps an existing key's position, so without it the map is FIFO wearing an LRU label. A disk read is not re-admitted, or any sequence of reads refills what eviction drained.
findings.riskOfFix: An evicted run costs a disk read per request. The test's real assertion is that its payload comes back byte-identical.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'an evicted run reads back off disk unchanged' (4 assertions)

findings.title: Two scopes read at once, and one of them vanished from disk
findings.repro: Open Key insights on a run that is not in ACTIVE. node test/flow.test.js :: 'two scopes read at once, both survive on disk' starts a second server over the same RI_DATA_DIR to reach that state.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-007-before.txt — '"all" was lost from disk; found ["checking"]'.
findings.rootCause: Each handler loadRun()s its own copy, writes its own scope into themesByScope, and saveRun()s the whole object. Last write wins; the lost scope is re-read and re-billed on the next open.
findings.fix: withRunLock() serialises per run id and updateRun() does read-modify-write through it, re-reading the record INSIDE the lock. Single-flight keyed on run AND scope is added alongside, because the same race has a cheaper form: two requests for the same scope were buying two model calls.
findings.riskOfFix: Writes to one run serialise. They are milliseconds; the model calls stay concurrent.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'two scopes read at once, both survive on disk' (3 assertions)

findings.title: 40 model calls could be in flight at once, and nothing said otherwise
findings.repro: node bughunt/logs/f008-concurrency-probe.mjs — 40 calls at a local endpoint that counts overlap.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-008-before.txt — 'peak in flight: 40'. After: 8, and 3 at RI_MODEL_CONCURRENCY=3.
findings.rootCause: extractCreatives caps 6 per advertiser and server.js runs every target in parallel, so the real ceiling was targets x 6 plus uncounted analysis calls.
findings.fix: A process-wide semaphore in createWithRetry(), the one function every model call goes through. release() hands its slot straight to the next waiter (a decrement-then-reacquire gap lets an unqueued caller jump in), and the retry loop holds its slot through backoff (releasing would drain the queue into the endpoint that just returned 429). The run records the limit and the observed peak, named observedPeakProcessWide because that is what it is.
findings.riskOfFix: A large capture takes longer. Latency, not correctness.
findings.testAdded: test/degraded.test.js :: 'no more model calls in flight than the process allows' (4 assertions)

findings.title: The cost line quoted the smaller of the two bills
findings.repro: POST /api/cost for any capture. node test/flow.test.js :: 'the cost quote states model spend, and never under-counts it'.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-009-before.txt — the quote says nothing about model calls. The screen read '1 request, 3 from cache' for a run about to buy up to thirty vision reads.
findings.rootCause: planCost reads the capture cache and stops. The extraction cache and the vision calls it does or does not save were never in the quote.
findings.fix: modelSpendFor() quotes fresh vision reads (upper-bounded by each advertiser's read cap, less transcriptions we can see are already held), extractions reused, the reader version the figures are about, Key insights as an explicitly excluded separate call, and two named booleans saying force bypasses the CAPTURE cache and not the EXTRACTION cache. The UI renders 'up to N', never a flat number.
findings.riskOfFix: The upper bound is loose on a cold cache (it is the cap, since the listing is not known until it is fetched). Quoting the midpoint would be a promise nobody can keep.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'the cost quote states model spend, and never under-counts it' (11 assertions, across nationals on/off, force on/off, client cached/not) + 4 browser assertions

findings.title: startCapture() had no try/catch; a failed POST disabled the only button forever
findings.repro: npm run test:ui :: 'the server is unreachable when Capture is pressed' — the journey aborts /api/capture at the network layer.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-010-F-015-F-016-before.txt. Not reachable from any test that existed, because the browser suite had never run.
findings.rootCause: The button was disabled on the way in and re-enabled on the line after the await, so anything that threw before that line left it disabled with an unhandled rejection and nothing on screen.
findings.fix: Both awaits guarded separately, because they fail differently and the user can act on the difference. An ok:true response with zero runs (every source refused) is handled too — reading runs[0] off an empty array is a TypeError that reads on screen as nothing happening.
findings.riskOfFix: None identified.
findings.testAdded: test/ui.test.js :: 'journey — the server is unreachable when Capture is pressed' (4 assertions)

findings.title: Health said the keys were set and called that ready
findings.repro: Point RI_DATA_DIR beneath a regular file and GET /api/health.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-011-before.txt — 'ok: expected false, got true' over a data directory that cannot be created.
findings.rootCause: Every capture ends in a write, and health checked only which API keys were present.
findings.fix: storageHealth() does a real write and delete, not a permission-bit inspection (a full disk and a read-only mount both pass an inspection and fail a write; a root process ignores the bits). Free space via statfs when it answers, reported as unknown when it does not. `ok` now means 'a capture run today would survive'. The landing page prints the failure beside the missing-key line.
findings.riskOfFix: A monitor keyed on health.ok will now go red on a full disk. That is the intended behaviour.
findings.testAdded: test/degraded.test.js :: 'health checks whether anything can actually be stored' (4 assertions)

findings.title: npm audit fix is a no-op here; the fix had to be pinned explicitly
findings.repro: npm audit fix, then npm audit.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-012-before.txt — 'up to date' followed by the same three advisories. express 4.22.2 and body-parser 1.20.6 both pin qs at ~6.15.1, entirely inside the vulnerable range; the patched release is 6.16.0.
findings.rootCause: npm prints 'fix available' because one exists in the registry, not because any range in the tree admits it.
findings.fix: An override pinning qs to ^6.16.0 — a minor bump inside the same major, against a maintainer range that predates the advisory. The alternative was express 5, a breaking major, for a moderate.
findings.riskOfFix: Stated plainly: if body-parser ever depends on 6.15-specific behaviour this override is where it breaks, and it is the first thing to remove when express ships a 4.x pinning a patched qs. Both suites pass on it.
findings.testAdded: none — npm audit is the assertion. bughunt/logs/91-npm-audit-after.txt: 0 vulnerabilities.

findings.title: A wrong reading was permanent until the whole extraction cache was retired
findings.repro: node test/degraded.test.js :: 'one creative can be re-read without retiring the whole cache'.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-013-before.txt — the route does not exist; the only lever was the reader version, which retires every extraction.
findings.rootCause: The cache is keyed on creativeId AND reader version, and only the version could invalidate. Hundreds of correct readings re-bought to fix one, so in practice nobody did, and the wrong reading stayed in the evidence drawer where it had been noticed.
findings.fix: POST /api/extraction/:creativeId/reread forgets one creative's stored reading. Costs nothing when called; the next capture pays for exactly one vision call. Without a reader argument it forgets every reading of that creative. The EVIDENCE bundle is untouched, with a test that says so. Calling twice is not an error. The id is validated before it reaches the filesystem.
findings.riskOfFix: An unauthenticated local endpoint that deletes cache entries. The app has no authentication by design (§4/§9); this deletes only a re-buyable transcription and never evidence.
findings.testAdded: test/degraded.test.js :: 'one creative can be re-read without retiring the whole cache' (6 assertions)

findings.title: "Display ads" was a claim about a network, made out of a filter on artwork
findings.repro: grep -rn display public/ lib/ README.md — see bughunt/logs/02-F-014-before.txt.
findings.evidence: SerpApi documents creative_format as 'text - Text, image - Image, video - Video' — the type of creative, not where it ran. And this repo's own atc-provider.js:9 records that there is no DISPLAY value in the provider's platform enum at all.
findings.rootCause: A filter on artwork type was labelled as a delivery network. Google's Transparency Center carries image creatives that ran on Discover, in Gmail, as YouTube companions and on Display, and the response does not distinguish them.
findings.fix: Every user-facing string now says image creatives / image ads: the source label, both mode cards, the scope bar, the nationals note, the client-wall empty state, two channel-shape sentences and the README's claim line. The source KEY google_display is unchanged — it is in every cache filename, every run.source and every snapshot, and renaming it would invalidate the cache and re-buy the captures. Model prompts are unchanged: they describe the picture to a reader, and touching one retires every extraction.
findings.riskOfFix: Two browser assertions matched the old label and were updated with it.
findings.testAdded: test/ui.test.js cost-line assertions; test/flow.test.js :: 'no count on this panel names a network the capture cannot establish'

findings.title: The client picker's dropdown covers the only other way in, and clicking it picks a client
findings.repro: Type a client name, clear the box, then click "Use a landing page instead". npm run test:ui :: 'the client picker never covers the only other way in'.
findings.evidence:
bughunt/logs/02-F-010-F-015-F-016-before.txt — '
Bank of Missouri
from
subtree intercepts pointer events'.
findings.rootCause: With an empty query, matchClients("") returns the first eight rows of a directory of forty and renders them as suggestions, overlaying the landing-page button. The rows handle mousedown and preventDefault() it, so the blur that would close the menu never fires: the click selects a client instead, and the next screen is scoped to one the user never chose.
findings.fix: An empty query closes the menu. Nothing was asked, so there is nothing to suggest.

findings.title: Wall filters outlived their run (H1, confirmed)
findings.repro: Filter the wall to one advertiser, press "Add a competitor", capture a set that does not contain them. npm run test:ui :: 'a second capture does not inherit the first one's filters'.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-010-F-015-F-016-before.txt. The second wall renders zero cards and reads as a capture that found nothing.
findings.rootCause: productFilter is re-adopted only 'if (S.productFilter == null)' and the advertiser filter was never cleared. "New analysis" hides this because it reloads the page; "Add a competitor" returns to the capture screen and captures again without one.
findings.fix: Both cleared when a capture starts. A filter is a view of a run, and this is a new run.
findings.riskOfFix: A user re-capturing with one extra competitor loses their chip selection. That is the correct behaviour: it is a different set.

findings.title: The one sentence at the top contradicted the card beneath it
findings.repro: node test/benchmark.test.js :: STAGE 11. A set where the client prints an APY and no competitor prints one, plus two nationals.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-017-before.txt — headline: 'Client CU holds the strongest advertised APY of the 4 comparable local competitors captured.' over a set where zero competitors printed one, with the client counted as the fourth. And differences: 'cash bonus (3 of 3), no monthly fee (3 of 3) and cash bonus (2 of 2)' — the (2 of 2) is the national set, unlabelled, inside a sentence headed 'Where competitors differ'.
findings.rootCause: TWO MEANINGS, ONE FIELD. `denominator` means comparable competitors in the ranked branch and brands-including-the-client in the sole-advertiser branch, and primary-read.js reads every finding as the first. Separately, the `pressure` list had no scope filter, so a national finding entered a local sentence — a rule this same file states, correctly, twenty lines below the defect.
findings.fix: findings.js marks the sole-advertiser branch `sole: true` rather than leaving it to be inferred from arithmetic. primary-read.js writes the sentence its evidence supports ('nobody else printed one, there is nothing to rank it against'), reports counts.comparableOnRate as 0 in that case, and filters nationals out of `pressure`.
findings.riskOfFix: The lead headline changes wording in the sole-advertiser case. It now agrees with the card below it.
findings.testAdded: test/benchmark.test.js :: STAGE 11 (9 assertions across findings, set shape, primary read, snapshot and coverage)

findings.title: An add-on's price was marked rankable at the fact level
findings.repro: node test/corpus-runner.js — CORPUS_ADDON_PRICE.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-018-before.txt — 'fact[monthly_fee].rankable: got true, expected false' for "$5.99/month with BaZing".
findings.rootCause: scopedToAddOn was enforced in rollUpBrand and not in the fact's own rankable flag. Two places decide whether an add-on price can be compared to a competitor's account fee, and only one of them knew.

findings.title: A 30-day snapshot was offered as the previous of a 90-day run
findings.repro: node test/flow.test.js :: 'a 30-day snapshot is not the previous of a 90-day run'. Capture at 30 days, then at 90; PEL3 stopped running 45 days ago so it sits between the two windows.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-020-before.txt — "Pelican State CU's cash bonus of $750 is newly observed since the September 2026 benchmark." It was not. The same ad had run for months and stopped 45 days ago; it was outside the narrower window and inside the wider one. The sentence reached the findings AND the primary read.
findings.rootCause: previousSnapshot() gated comparability on client + product + source. The window was written onto every snapshot and read by nothing.
findings.fix: The window joins the gate and is recorded as a number, not only as two dates, so comparability is never inferred from timestamps a daylight-saving boundary can shift. snapshotWindowDays() derives it for snapshots written before the field existed — almost all of them — so no existing month-over-month comparison is lost. Fails closed: a candidate whose window cannot be established is not offered. A day of tolerance absorbs DST; it is not wide enough to let 30 meet 60.
findings.riskOfFix: A client who changes window loses their delta for one cycle. That is the correct outcome: the two captures are not comparable.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'a 30-day snapshot is not the previous of a 90-day run' (5 assertions). test/fixture-lab.js gained a served-window filter and PEL3, without which the whole class was untestable.

findings.title: A failed artwork download read as a competitor who is not advertising
findings.repro: node test/flow.test.js :: 'H11 — three different losses in one run', with RI_MOCK_IMG_403=1.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-021-before.txt — the target reports status 'empty' with reason undefined. On screen that is the same as a competitor who simply is not running ads.
findings.rootCause: capture() returns ok:true with an empty images array when every download fails, and set no reason. The empty-LISTING path above it already distinguishes 'preview_only' from 'no_ads'; this path said nothing.
findings.fix: An empty capture names which of the three happened — download_failed, preview_only or no_ads — and the UI has words for the new one. 'We could not fetch their artwork' is a fact about our capture; 'they are not advertising' is a claim about them.
findings.riskOfFix: None identified. The field is present only when there is nothing to show.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'the screen says which kind of nothing this is'

findings.title: The national age caveat has never once fired
findings.repro: node test/flow.test.js :: 'H19 — the national age caveat appears exactly when it should'. Age a national cache entry to 60 days and read the board over a 30-day window.
findings.evidence: bughunt/logs/02-F-022-before.txt — grep -c referenceNote lib/analyze.js returns 0. The caveat appends to bm.referenceNote, which buildBenchmark() has never produced, so the condition read undefined on every run in the product's history.
findings.rootCause: The caveat was written against the audit table's object instead of the board's. The note that exists is the snapshot's referenceNote, which is what the reference block carries and what snapshotHtml() renders.
findings.fix: Moved into boardFor(), onto the note the UI actually renders. Tested three ways, because a caveat that always fires is wallpaper and one that never fires is a lie: silent on a same-day capture, present with the age and the window on a 60-day-old capture read over 30 days, silent again on that same capture read over 90.
findings.riskOfFix: The caveat now appears where it never did. That is the fix, and the wording was already written to be honest about it: 'may fall outside'.
findings.testAdded: test/flow.test.js :: 'H19 — the national age caveat appears exactly when it should' (8 assertions)

notAttempted.why: Pagination. Explicitly out of scope per §4 — implementing it changes spend. The exposure is audited in REPORT.md instead: every sentence leaning on national absence already reads as an observation about the capture, and the cross-cutting sweep now checks that automatically.

The corpus replay needs one Haiku vision call per creative and §10 requires approval first. It also needs creatives: runs/ is gitignored, so _evidence is empty in a clone. The runner refuses without RI_CORPUS_APPROVED=1 and --dry-run prints the exact count, currently 0. Nothing else is blocking it.
Deployment-conditional and disabled. The work order says to start it only if deployment is explicitly in scope, and it is not.

newSuspicions.title: The fresh-vision-read upper bound is very loose on a cold cache
newSuspicions.why: modelSpendFor quotes each fetching advertiser at its full read cap, because the listing is unknown until it is fetched. With nationals on that reads 'up to 380 fresh creative reads' where a real run will do a fraction of it. It never under-counts, which is the rule — but a quote a strategist learns to ignore is a quote that has stopped working. A median-from-history figure shown BESIDE the upper bound would fix it without weakening the guarantee.

newSuspicions.title: The findings board sits below the fold at 1366x768
newSuspicions.why: Measured, not guessed: the first .fcard sits at y=794 on a 768px screen, because the eyebrow, title, sampling note, persistence warning, funnel and stats all come first. That is the screen-share size in §7. Whether the ordering is right is a design call I have no mandate to make, so the browser test asserts only that the board is laid out and reachable, and records the number.

newSuspicions.title: primaryRead relabels the set shape's 'captured brands' as 'local advertisers'
newSuspicions.why: set-shape.js says '3 of 4 captured brands advertise one' — a denominator that includes the client, stated as such. The primary read renders it as 'the figure most local advertisers print (3 of 4)'. Defensible, because the client IS a local advertiser, and it is the same class of relabelling that produced F-017. Left alone because I could not establish it says anything false.

newSuspicions.title: isCompleteFigure() accepts a percent with no unit context
newSuspicions.why: A raw of '5.5%' on a metric whose unit is percent passes completeness, but '5.5% off' and '5.5% APY' are different facts and only the RATE_REDUCTION regex separates them. A figure printed as a bare percentage next to no word at all would be counted as the metric the model named it. The corpus is the place to pin this down with a real creative.

newSuspicions.title: The extraction cache is written per creative with no bound
newSuspicions.why: prune() exists and is documented as 'only ever called explicitly' — and nothing calls it. F-006 bounded memory; disk is still unbounded, and the extraction cache is the thing that grows fastest. F-011 now reports free space, so at least it becomes visible before it becomes a failure.

newSuspicions.title: No test asserts that a refused comparability reason reaches the UI
newSuspicions.why: This is H6, listed as not attempted. Raising it here too because the failure mode is a silently blank cell, which looks identical to 'not observed' and means something completely different.

newSuspicions.title: findPreviousRun() still does not gate on the window
newSuspicions.why: F-020 fixed previousSnapshot(), which is what the BOARD reads. findPreviousRun() — which feeds run.diff, the 'still running / newly appeared / no longer observed' strip — gates on client, mode, source and product, and not on days. The same 30-vs-90 mismatch is therefore still available to that strip. It counts creative ids rather than figures, so the damage is smaller and the wording ('no longer observed') is already correctly hedged, but it is the same defect and it is one line from the same fix.

newSuspicions.title: The fixture market had no window dimension until this branch
newSuspicions.why: listingFor() returned every row whatever start_date was asked for, so a 30-day and a 90-day capture came back identical and every window-shaped bug was untestable — which is why F-020 survived. It filters now, and PEL3 sits between the two windows, but ONE row is thin: a second, on a different advertiser and a different product, would let the window interact with product scope and with the national tier.
